items.note: Field experiment randomly assigning technology-consulting employees to LLM assistance or none; supervisor and external-evaluator creativity ratings rose, more for employees high in metacognitive strategies. N not in the abstract (search notes say 250); ratings are of employee creativity, so check whether they score specific outputs; SSRN version 10.2139/ssrn.5864662 is the same study; the claimed after-AI finding needs a full-text check.

Within-subjects user study (N=12) of VeriForge, an AI system that helps fiction writers discover domain knowledge, against a baseline condition; expert raters judged domain grounding of passages. The outcome is grounding rather than creativity, the baseline condition is not described, and the sample is far below 50.

Study 1 probes cultural bias in ChatGPT and ErnieBot (model only); Study 2 is an experiment in which culturally aligned versus misaligned user-AI pairs produced creative solutions rated for novelty and usefulness (an AI-configuration comparison, not AI versus no AI); Study 3 is a field dyad survey. N not in the abstract (search notes say 385 in Study 2); assignment not described.

Quasi-experiment in three middle-school classes (45, 41, 45 students) comparing computer-assisted teaching with generative-AI-assisted teaching with and without teacher supervision; outcomes are a knowledge test, satisfaction, and engagement, with no creativity outcome (it appears in Shi 2026's creativity meta-analysis anyway).

Between-group experiment with 202 German participants in human-human dyads, human-Internet, or two human-ChatGPT conditions (basic or specific instructions) on alternate-uses, consequences, and problem-solving tasks; human dyads scored highest on divergent thinking, with human and automated (Ocsai) scoring. Assignment procedure not stated in the abstract.

One-group pretest-posttest design: 31 undergraduates used ChatGPT for assignments for 10 weeks, with CREA creativity test before and after; no evidence of decline. No control group and below 50 participants, so likely excluded; the post-test is plausibly without AI (after_ai), but the abstract does not say.

Quasi-experiment with two independent groups of 56 undergraduates on a creative reinterpretation task, one group allowed GenAI in the analytical phases before creative production; rubric-scored creative performance did not differ significantly. Abstract from the Pegaso IRIS repository record; venue and DOI not identified.

81 university students produced texts as humans alone, with Gemini alone, and in human-AI collaboration under four prompt strategies; texts were scored for lexical diversity, discourse structure, and student-rated quality and originality. Design (within-person, order) and assignment are unclear; the AI-only arm is an AI-versus-human comparison.

Crowd workers on a text summarization task under conditions that discourage LLM use (instructions, disabled copy-paste); secondary analyses find LLM use yields high-quality but homogeneous responses. The task is not creative and the homogeneity contrast is detected LLM users versus non-users, so it may belong in context_observational or out; CACM version of arXiv 2310.15683.

Difference-in-differences on a matched panel of incumbent YouTube creators using the US-versus-Europe rollout of the Inspiration Tab idea tool; access raised output 4.1 percent and made creators' videos more similar to their own prior work, with no change in similarity across creators. SSRN working paper.
